g1.label: 1. Vast, wild ___
g1.why: The text describes Canada as famous for its vast, wild landscapes.

g2.label: 2. Warmed almost ___ times faster
g2.why: The text says the Canadian Arctic has warmed almost three times faster than the global average.

g3.label: 3. The sea ice has become ___
g3.why: The text says the sea ice has become thinner as the climate warms.

g4.label: 4. ___ peoples have protected the land
g4.why: The text says Indigenous peoples have protected the land for thousands of years.

g5.label: 5. New national ___
g5.why: The text says the government has created new national parks.

g6.label: 6. Joined climate ___
g6.why: The text says many young people have joined climate marches.

g7.label: 7. Cleaner ___
g7.why: The text says companies have started to use cleaner energy, such as wind power.

g8.label: 8. One of Canada's biggest ___
g8.why: The text says protecting the environment is one of Canada's biggest challenges.

g1.label: 1. Temperatures ___ sharply (rise)
g1.why: ‘In recent years’ signals an action continuing to now, so the present perfect ‘have risen’ is used.

g2.label: 2. In 2019, Canada ___ (declare)
g2.why: ‘In 2019’ is a finished, specific past time, so the simple past ‘declared’ is used.

g3.label: 3. Indigenous peoples ___ the land (protect)
g3.why: ‘For thousands of years’ signals an action continuing to now, so the present perfect ‘have protected’ is used.

g4.label: 4. The sea ice ___ thinner (become)
g4.why: ‘Since the 1980s’ signals an action continuing to now, so the present perfect ‘has become’ is used.

g5.label: 5. Last summer, wildfires ___ (destroy)
g5.why: ‘Last summer’ is a finished, specific past time, so the simple past ‘destroyed’ is used.

g6.label: 6. Scientists ___ the Arctic (study)
g6.why: ‘For many decades’ signals an action continuing to now, so the present perfect ‘have studied’ is used.

g7.label: 7. So far, the government ___ parks (create)
g7.why: ‘So far’ signals an action continuing to now, so the present perfect ‘has created’ is used.

g8.label: 8. Two years ago, she ___ (join)
g8.why: ‘Two years ago’ is a finished, specific past time, so the simple past ‘joined’ is used.

g1.label: 1. The ice has ___ started to melt
g1.why: ‘Already’ is used in positive present perfect sentences to show something has happened sooner than expected.

g2.label: 2. Have you ___ visited a park?
g2.why: ‘Ever’ is used in present perfect questions asking about experience.

g3.label: 3. I have ___ seen the lights
g3.why: ‘Never’ (= not at any time) is the standard present perfect word for talking about experience.

g4.label: 4. Protected these forests ___ 1885
g4.why: ‘Since’ introduces a specific starting point in time, not a duration like ‘for’.

g5.label: 5. Studied the ice ___ a century
g5.why: ‘For’ introduces a duration of time, not a starting point like ‘since’.

g6.label: 6. Has not reached its goals ___
g6.why: ‘Yet’ is used at the end of negative present perfect sentences to show something hasn't happened.

g7.label: 7. We have ___ finished planting
g7.why: ‘Just’ shows an action finished a very short time ago.

g8.label: 8. The warmest winter they have ___ recorded
g8.why: ‘Ever’ is used after superlatives in the present perfect.
